subject: botany_2
question_text: Which tissue transports photosynthates? What experiment proves this?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The tissue
steps.margin_note: Name the tissue and what it carries. Add the word translocation.
lines: PHLOEM is the tissue that transports
photosynthates (the food made in the leaves).
steps.why: Phloem carries the products of photosynthesis while xylem carries water, and separating the two tissues by what they carry is the point of the question.
common_mistakes: Naming xylem. Xylem carries water and minerals; PHLOEM carries food.
Leaving out the word photosynthates or food. The tissue is named by what it carries.
steps.memory_tip: Phloem carries food; xylem carries water.

steps.label: The experiment
steps.margin_note: Name it, say what is removed, and say where the swelling appears.

lines.text: Ringing: remove the phloem and food stops

lines: The RINGING or GIRDLING experiment proves it.
A ring of bark, containing the phloem, is removed
The part ABOVE the ring swells, because food
collects there and cannot move down.
steps.why: Removing only the phloem and watching food pile up above the cut is direct evidence that the phloem was the route, because the xylem was left intact.
common_mistakes: Naming no experiment. Ringing or girdling is the named answer.
Saying the part below swells. The swelling is ABOVE the ring.
steps.memory_tip: Cut the phloem and the food stops above the cut.
